module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 726

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/726](https://www.erdosproblems.com/726)
- [EGRS75] Erdős, P., and Graham, R. L. and Ruzsa, I. Z. and Straus, E. G., On the prime factors of
  $(\sp{2n}\sb{n})$. Math. Comp. (1975), 83-92.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Nat Filter Finset
open scoped Topology Asymptotics

namespace Erdos726

/--
As $n\to \infty$ ranges over integers
$\sum_{p\leq n}1_{n\in (p/2,p)\pmod{p}}\frac{1}{p}\sim \frac{\log\log n}{2}$?

A conjecture of Erdős, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus [EGRS75].

By $n\in (p/2,p)\pmod{p}$ we mean $n\equiv r\pmod{p}$ for some integer $r$ with $p/2<r<p$.
The remainder `n % p` is computed in `ℕ` before casting to `ℝ`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_726 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ ∑ p ∈ (range (n + 1)).filter
          (fun p : ℕ ↦ p.Prime ∧ (p : ℝ) / 2 < ((n % p : ℕ) : ℝ)),
        (1 : ℝ) / (p : ℝ))
      ~[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ)) / 2) := by
  sorry

/--
The classical estimate of Mertens states that $\sum_{p\leq n}\frac{1}{p}\sim \log\log n$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_726.variants.mertens_estimate :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ ∑ p ∈ (range (n + 1)).filter (fun p ↦ p.Prime), (1 : ℝ) / ((p : ℕ) : ℝ))
    ~[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ))) := by
  sorry

end Erdos726

reformulations.difference: The source describes an integer residue r congruent to n modulo p with p/2 < r < p. Lean filters using only the lower bound (p : ℝ) / 2 < ↑(n % p).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For prime p, p > 0, so n % p is the unique congruent integer in [0,p). Any source witness r lies in this interval because p/2 > 0. Consequently r must equal n % p, and the omitted upper bound follows automatically from Nat.mod_lt. The residue predicates and the resulting sums agree exactly. This equivalence, including the existential integer witness and equality of the sums, was proved without sorry in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.
